workflow_harden_citation.verdict: PARTIAL_EXECUTION (remote verification DEFERRED per Hard Constraint -- all 20 workflows are deliberately disabled)
workflow_harden_citation.summary: S-115 static review of all 20 workflows, 8-dimension probe each. 3 HIGH-severity concurrency-guard defects found and FIXED this sprint (content-governance-checks.yml, llms-generation.yml, skill-governance.yml -- the confirmed top 3 real cost drivers, 75.7% of total usage combined). 1 additional HIGH finding (upstream-monitor.yml, a broken failure chain -- originally believed tied to a PAT gap/issue #94, CORRECTED 2026-09-18: actually a missing-clone-cache bug in repo_patrol.py's cmd_sweep(), fixed in commit 72821fbb4a, no human decision or credential was ever needed) is now RESOLVED, not deferred. 10 further MEDIUM/LOW findings recorded, mostly deferred as low-cost-impact or requiring a policy/human decision (zero SHA-pinned actions repo-wide; 5 workflows with possibly-dead PR triggers; an undocumented schedule collision; two audit-step/regression-step unguarded-consumption patterns). Full detail: reports/sprint/workflow-harden-2026-09-17/final_verdict.md and preflight/hidden_problems.json. Cite, do not re-derive.

workflows.name: Content Governance Checks
workflows.notes: SUSPECTED #1 COST DRIVER. Full Hugo build, ~30 steps, path filter covers content/**, scripts/pipeline/**, scripts/ci/**, skills/**, themes/**, layouts/**. NO concurrency/cancel-in-progress block. ~266 commits touched content/ in the first 16 days of September 2026 alone. TWO-STEP FIX (updated 2026-09-16, user-directed): (1) add concurrency: {group: content-governance-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true} via /workflow-harden FIRST -- more critical on self-hosted than GitHub-hosted since one physical machine has no elastic parallelism; (2) self-host on this dev machine (WSL2 + fresh Docker container per job) to reduce this workflow's GitHub-hosted-minute cost to zero. Public migration was never available (push(main)-gated, needs native required-check integration) -- self-hosting is the only lever beyond in-place optimization. Low code-injection risk: this repo's real flow is direct push, not PR-from-fork.

workflows.name: Cross-Repo Index Sync

workflows.name: Example Verification Tests
workflows.notes: Runs the full suite twice, once per OS, on every matching push. Path filter narrow (~6 files under scripts/pipeline/lib/example_verification/**) so absolute cost is probably small, but Windows minutes cost ~1.7-2x Linux. Confirm in TC-05 whether the suite actually asserts CRLF/OS-sensitive behavior; if not, demote the Windows leg to schedule/dispatch like skill-governance.yml's soft launch.

workflows.name: Skill Governance
workflows.notes: SUSPECTED #2 COST DRIVER. Windows job is continue-on-error:true (soft-launched) but runs the SAME ~50-entry broad path filter as the required Linux job -- broad filter x duplicate OS is a compounding multiplier. UPDATED 2026-09-16 (user-directed): self-host the required Linux job on this dev machine (WSL2 + container), same rationale as content-governance-checks.yml (push-gated, public migration unavailable, low code-injection risk since this repo's flow is direct push not PR-from-fork). The Windows leg is a separate, deferred decision -- self-hosting it natively is mechanically simpler (host is already Windows, no WSL2 layer needed) but gives up GitHub-hosted Windows runners' VM-disposability for a narrow, soft-launched job; decide from TC-04's real usage share (if small, leave on GitHub-hosted; if meaningful, self-host inside its own isolated, hard-timeout container rather than running it loose on the desktop).

self_host_primary_candidates.note: UPDATED 2026-09-16 (user-directed): these two are the suspected #1 and #2 cost drivers, and public migration is structurally unavailable to both (push(main)-gated, need native required-check integration). Self-hosting on this dev machine (WSL2 + fresh container per job, dedicated runner label) is the only lever that reduces their GitHub-hosted-minute cost to zero, beyond in-place optimization.
